root_idea.summary: A weakening or relaxation of intensity: what is forceful becomes less vigorous, still, gentle, or weak.
root_idea.development: The root develops from remission after vehemence to slackness in activity, bodily or perceptual weakness, and the cessation or interval that follows exertion or intense action. Its causative forms denote making something abate or weak.

senses.definition: To slacken, abate, or become still after intensity; to cease from vigorous activity.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is an intransitive description of sustained activity: the angels do not slacken from their energetic worship.

senses.definition: To cause something to slacken, abate, or become less intense; to weaken it.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is passive and concerns something not being made less intense or relieved; the causative relation is expressed by the Form II morphology.

senses.definition: An interval or cessation between messengers, during which the prophetic mission is absent.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the interval is specifically between messengers and is associated with the cessation or effacement of their mission and religious signs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become physically languid or weak, with laxity in the joints; also, of the eyelids or gaze, to become languid and lacking sharpness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This branch is applied to the body, limbs, eyelids, or gaze; a languid gaze may be regarded as aesthetically pleasing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To measure by a fitr, the span between the extended thumb and forefinger.
To render a person or body languid, faint, or weak, with laxity of the joints.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cause may be a beverage, disease, or intoxication; the object may be left unexpressed with افْتَرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cloud, to become motionless after raining, either while prepared to discharge rain or after discharging its water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of a rain cloud that ceases moving after its rain-bearing activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to refrain from covering so that its seminal fluid collects.
A palm-leaf implement resembling a sufrah, used for sifting flour or meal.
The span between the tip of the thumb and the tip of the forefinger when they are extended apart in the customary manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional unit of measurement; its plural is أَفْتَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Languor, remissness, weakness, feebleness, or faintness; a state of reduced strength after activity or force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general nominal sense, distinct from the Quranic technical sense of an interval between messengers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To settle or rest toward something after a period of energetic exertion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction in which إلى marks what one settles or rests toward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A speckled torpedo fish, said to induce languor in the legs of a person who treads on it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological term referring to the electric fish found in the Nile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Languor that marks the beginning of intoxication.
The soft, raised parts of the frogs of horses' hooves.
Lukewarm or tepid, especially of water that has ceased to be hot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مَاءٌ فَاتِرٌ for water between hot and cold.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Languid, weak-looking, or lacking sharpness; said of the gaze, and also of weak walking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of the eye, the weakness may be a soft or aesthetically pleasing languor; of walking, it denotes weakness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beverage that renders its drinker languid or weak, sometimes with laxity of the joints.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Lane reports competing readings for the term; the usage is associated with a beverage producing bodily languor.
